subject: Private Observability: export pipeline and tracing hooks for VPC deployments

Subject: Private Observability: export pipeline and tracing hooks for VPC deployments

Hi all,

Following up from last week's call — Acme needs a concrete plan for how Redwood Private (VPC) will surface logs, metrics, and traces to their SIEM and tracing backend without opening broad egress. Goals: encrypted transport, controllable push points inside their VPC, minimal footprint on their side, and full auditability (who/when).

Key constraints from Acme (Jen):
- No public internet egress for raw logs allowed.
- Only TLS mutual-auth endpoints reachable over peered connection or private interconnect.
- Retention/PII concerns: they want first-line scrubbing before export where possible.

Options we discussed on the call:
A) Push via a customer-managed collector (Fluent Bit/Fluentd) inside their VPC -> push to Acme SIEM over private peering (CEF/Syslog over TLS).
B) Push to a middle-tier Kafka/topic in the VPC that their SIEM pulls from via a connector.
C) Export metrics via Prometheus remote_write to a gateway inside the VPC, traces via OTLP/OTel Collector with mTLS.

Attachments: an architecture sketch (observability-export-arch.v1.pdf) and a sample header-only log (sample-logs-headers.txt) to show which fields we export by default.

Ask: can Peter and Jen confirm which SIEM ingestion protocols they prefer (CEF over TLS, Syslog-TLS, or Kafka connect)? Dev, Hiro — reasonability check on the proposed push endpoints and whether we should prefer OTLP over HTTP/gRPC for traces in the private setup.

I'll collate answers and produce a short spec for approvals.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Platform Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah — quick notes from the SIEM side.

We support all three ingestion models but in order of operational simplicity for customers:
1) CEF over TLS (TCP/6514) to a managed collector inside the VPC — simplest if Acme wants immediate parity with Splunk/QRadar.
2) Kafka topic(s) with connector pull — useful for buffering and replay, but requires topic management and ACLs.
3) Syslog TLS — acceptable but CEF preserves structured fields better for parity with existing parsers.

Security: mutual TLS with client certs + CN validation is standard for us. We can provide certs or accept Acme's internal CA-signed certs. For OTLP traces, gRPC over mTLS to an OTel Collector inside the VPC is recommended.

Operational tip: if you (Redwood) are doing any pre-scrubbing, prefer doing it in the collector (Fluent Bit) inside the VPC before sending out; that keeps audit trails on the customer side.

Happy to help produce a sample CEF ingestion guide and a reference Fluent Bit config.

- Peter
Peter Liu
Integrations Lead, InfraOps

Adding engineering details and feasibility notes — TL;DR: all options doable; recommend a two-phase rollout (collector-first, then add buffered Kafka for heavy ingest).

Implementation notes:
- Traces: we'll expose OTLP endpoints on a customer-contained OTel Collector (gRPC) listening on a private IP. Collector authenticates using mTLS to the downstream SIEM/tracing endpoint. We will ship a sample collector config; this allows Adapters (Jaeger/Tempo) to be swapped by Acme.
- Logs: Fluent Bit as a lightweight in-VPC forwarder. Suggest default pipeline: application -> redact plugin (PII ruleset) -> format to CEF -> tcp_out plugin -> TLS (mutual). Example snippet:
  [OUTPUT]
  Name tcp
  Match *
  Host 10.2.5.10
  Port 6514
  TLS On
  TLS.Verify On
  TLS.CA_File /etc/ssl/acme/ca.pem
  TLS.Client_Cert /etc/ssl/redwood/client.crt
  TLS.Client_Key /etc/ssl/redwood/client.key

- Metrics: Prometheus remote_write to an in-VPC push gateway; we can also support scraping by an Acme-managed Prometheus via VPC peering. We'll expose label conventions and cardinality limits.
- Networking: require a single allowed egress to Acme-specified collector IP(s) and ports (no 0.0.0.0/0). For managed routing we can use interface endpoint + route table entries in the peered VPC.
- Audit: We will record an export event in Redwood audit logs (who triggered, job id, batch id) and surface that in console. Those audit logs themselves can be exported via the same mechanism or via a secure API pull.

Open questions for Acme/Security:
1) Will Acme host the collector endpoint (preferred) or accept a Redwood-managed endpoint in their private network?
2) Do they require tokenized envelopes (signed attestations) on exported batches?

Next steps: I can produce a reference Fluent Bit + OTel Collector repo and a network ACL file. Estimate: 2 engineer-days to draft configs and 1 day for testing with InfraOps sample.

Thanks,

Thanks everyone — quick summary & decision items for the spec doc: 

Decisions:
- Default approach: Collector-first. Acme to host Fluent Bit / OTel Collector in their VPC. Redwood will provide reference configs and a pre-approved PII redaction rule set.
- Ingestion protocol: CEF over TLS (TCP/6514) for logs; OTLP (gRPC) with mTLS for traces; Prometheus remote_write for metrics. InfraOps to own ingestion docs.
- Network posture: single IP/port egress (customer-provided collector IPs). No public internet for raw exports.

Action items:
- Dev: produce reference Fluent Bit + OTel Collector repo + sample network ACLs. (ETA: 2 business days)
- Peter: provide CEF ingestion guide and sample cert provisioning steps. (ETA: 3 business days)
- Jen/Acme: confirm collector IP(s) and whether they want Redwood-managed certs or to use their CA. (ETA: EOD Wednesday)
- Hannah/Evelyn: draft short runbook for on-call escalation if export failures occur (who to page at Acme and Redwood).

I'll take these and produce a 1-page spec for approvals by EOD tomorrow. If anyone has other risks (compliance, retention windows, KMS use for signing), flag them now.

— Hiro

Director, Product Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
